excluded: complete TCP and generic Reno conformance
limited transmit and automatic new-data emission on duplicate ACK
idle restart, ECN/SACK/NewReno and multiple-loss recovery guarantees
FIN-only fast retransmit and legacy FIN wire-window knowledge
universal byte/output/timing and interpreter/translator/implementation refinement proof

CONN-OPEN.interpretation: Select ISS; active OPEN enters SYN-SENT, passive OPEN enters LISTEN.

CONN-LISTEN.interpretation: A SYN in LISTEN initializes receive state and emits SYN+ACK; ACK-bearing input emits RST; RST is ignored.

CONN-SYN-SENT.interpretation: Validate ACK before processing SYN/RST; valid SYN+ACK establishes, bare SYN enters SYN-RECEIVED.

CONN-SIMULTANEOUS.interpretation: Figure 7: active vs passive origin is retained in SYN-RECEIVED; simultaneous SYN+ACK completes synchronization.

CONN-ACK.interpretation: In-order ACK completes synchronization or acknowledges FIN, with per-state transitions.

CONN-FIN.interpretation: FIN consumes one receive sequence number, is acknowledged, and changes per-state close progression.

CONN-CLOSE.interpretation: CLOSE in ESTABLISHED or CLOSE-WAIT emits FIN and enters FIN-WAIT-1 or LAST-ACK; repeated close does not emit a second FIN.

CONN-ABORT.interpretation: ABORT sends RST in the specified synchronized states; other states discard the TCB without output RST.

CONN-RESET.interpretation: Exact RCV.NXT resets the connection; passive SYN-RECEIVED returns to LISTEN, active origin closes.

CONN-CLOSED-INPUT.interpretation: CLOSED ignores resets and emits a correctly formatted reset for other control segments.

CONN-TIMEOUT.interpretation: User timeout deletes the TCB; retransmission timeout repeats oldest outstanding segment; TIME-WAIT timeout closes.

RTO-PROFILE.interpretation: Use 1000ms initial SYN RTO and exponential doubling for control retransmission. After a SYN timeout use at least 3000ms for subsequent FIN, retaining a larger backed-off value; no RTT estimator is modeled.

CONNECTION-PROFILE.interpretation: Inherited single-connection control paths retain validated control shapes, exact sequence checks and configurable user/MSL deadlines. The data extension supersedes the base zero-payload assumption only in ESTABLISHED, within the explicit DATA-SCOPE boundary; data in other lifecycle states remains excluded.

DATA-SEQ.interpretation: Each new data octet consumes one sequence number; cumulative ACK removes an acknowledged prefix. Retransmission does not advance SND.NXT.

DATA-ACK.interpretation: New ACKs satisfy SND.UNA < SEG.ACK <= SND.NXT; duplicate and old ACKs do not remove data; future ACK triggers an ACK.

DATA-WINDOW.interpretation: Update SND.WND only for acceptable ACK and newer WL1/WL2. Segmentation respects the available advertised send window.

DATA-RECEIVE.interpretation: Accept and trim text overlapping the receive window; advance RCV.NXT only over contiguous newly accepted bytes, ACK the next expected octet.

DATA-SEND.interpretation: Model buffers application octets and segments them within the configured capacity, MSS and send window.

DATA-RTX.interpretation: The retransmission timer sends the oldest outstanding data again. This profile uses fixed initial RTO and exponential backoff only.

DATA-RTO.interpretation: Start on first outstanding transmission, restart on new partial ACK, cancel on all acknowledged, retransmit oldest on expiry and double RTO (5.1-5.6). No RTT sampling or maximum retry policy.

DATA-SCOPE.interpretation: Inherit finite buffers/connection and explicit reassembly, expand accepted ACK+payload/window composition and shrinking windows; first accepted byte wins, raw accepted SEG.SEQ used for WL1. Only ESTABLISHED, no FIN data or full recovery/persist implementation.

RX-QUEUE.interpretation: Retain higher sequence-number payload in the finite receive window (SHLD-31); process the entire contiguous queued prefix before one ACK (MUST-59).

RX-WINDOW.interpretation: Apply Table 6 nonempty-payload acceptability: positive receive window and first or last payload sequence within the offered interval. Trim accepted data to that interval.

RX-SEQUENCE.interpretation: Advance RCV.NXT only by contiguous newly accepted octets, modulo 2^32, with no repeated application delivery.

RX-SCOPE.interpretation: Inherit finite buffers/connection and explicit reassembly, expand accepted ACK+payload/window composition and shrinking windows; first accepted byte wins, raw accepted SEG.SEQ used for WL1. Only ESTABLISHED, no FIN data or full recovery/persist implementation.

SEG-ORDER.interpretation: Validate receive sequence first; reject unacceptable segments before ACK/window processing; process ACK/window before text. Future ACK causes ACK+drop; old ACK does not discard accepted payload.

SEG-ACK.interpretation: Cumulative ACK removes acknowledged retransmission prefix. Full ACK cancels rtx, new partial ACK restarts it, duplicate/old ACK leaves its deadline. ACK-only valid segments do not cause ACK loops.

SEG-WINDOW.interpretation: Update advertised peer window only for SND.UNA <= SEG.ACK <= SND.NXT with fresh WL1/WL2; SEG.SEQ uses the original accepted wire header in this profile.

SEG-SHRINK.interpretation: Sender remains robust when the usable window becomes negative (MUST-34). No new data is sent beyond the current window; retransmit oldest outstanding data within the positive window (SHLD-15/16).

SEG-ZERO-FLIGHT.interpretation: With outstanding data and zero peer window, the existing timeout sends one oldest octet as a probe and backs off. Zero window with only unsent data still requires the later persist mechanism.

SEG-SCOPE.interpretation: Inherit finite buffers/connection and explicit reassembly, expand accepted ACK+payload/window composition and shrinking windows; first accepted byte wins, raw accepted SEG.SEQ used for WL1. Only ESTABLISHED, no FIN data or full recovery/persist implementation.

CL-QUEUE.interpretation: Queue CLOSE after preceding SENDs are segmentized. Active close enters FIN-WAIT-1 immediately. FIN consumes one sequence number after data; repeat close must not consume another.

CL-ACK.interpretation: Process ACK before text/FIN, remove acknowledged data prefix and independently acknowledge FIN. FIN-WAIT-1 advances only when its FIN is acknowledged; CLOSING then enters TIME-WAIT, LAST-ACK enters CLOSED.

CL-HALF.interpretation: Read previously accepted data through half-close; receive text during FIN-WAIT-1/2. Peer FIN does not erase outstanding local data; CLOSE-WAIT can still send before local close.

CL-TIMER.interpretation: Data and FIN share one retransmission timer; preserve its deadline when adding FIN to an existing flight. Partial ACK restarts, full ACK cancels. Retransmit oldest data before FIN without consuming sequence space.

CL-SCOPE.interpretation: Finite 16-octet queues; separate FIN-only event with implicit unchanged peer window. Out-of-order FIN is ACKed/dropped and must be retransmitted; FIN+payload and no-flight persist remain pending. app.transmit explicitly schedules queued bytes/FIN.

FIN-SPACE.interpretation: SEG.LEN includes FIN control octet after all payload. A FIN marker is separate from the byte buffer and is acknowledged exactly once.

FIN-QUEUE.interpretation: Queue acceptable ahead FIN until all preceding bytes become contiguous; drain text and FIN before one cumulative ACK (Table 6, MUST-59). FIN outside the offered receive interval is trimmed and must be retransmitted.

FIN-WINDOW.interpretation: Explicit FIN-segment headers use existing sequence-before-ACK and WL1/WL2 window processing before text/FIN; unacceptable sequence or future ACK cannot consume or install FIN.

FIN-CLOSE.interpretation: After contiguous FIN consumption enter CLOSE-WAIT, CLOSING or TIME-WAIT as appropriate, including own FIN acknowledged in the same segment; duplicate FIN cannot deliver EOF twice and restarts TIME-WAIT only at the already consumed FIN position.

FIN-SCOPE.interpretation: Single shared 16-byte receive queue and one FIN marker. First accepted marker wins for contradictory FIN positions; queued bytes at/after that EOF are discarded. Legacy net.fin has no observed window/payload; net.fin_segment is the complete declared FIN header event.

RTT-ALG.interpretation: Exact rational SRTT/RTTVAR; update variance from old SRTT before smoothing SRTT with alpha=1/8 beta=1/4. Round RTO upward to integer ms, G=1ms, minimum 1000ms and optional maximum 60000ms.

RTT-KARN.interpretation: One outstanding sample anchored to an original segment end. Mark it ambiguous only when retransmitted sequence space overlaps its unacknowledged interval; never sample ambiguous ACKs. A fresh transmission may replace an ambiguous sample.

RTT-TIMER.interpretation: Start/preserve/restart/cancel one timer for byte and SYN/FIN flight. Recompute before a new ACK restart; backoff by two up to 60s. Keep inherited post-SYN-timeout lower-bound configuration until a valid sample arrives.

RTT-SCOPE.interpretation: Single connection with exact rational estimator and 1ms virtual clock. Samples include SYN, new data and FIN; partial ACK cannot complete the sample before its end. Existing finite buffers/sequence assumptions remain. This does not implement congestion or all recovery.

TX-HISTORY.interpretation: Record last transmission time for each finite in-flight data octet and FIN. A timer retransmission includes only the oldest contiguous prefix whose octets have aged at least the current pre-backoff RTO; retransmitted bytes receive the current clock. If oldest byte/FIN is not yet eligible, wait for its deadline without backoff or false emission.

TX-SCOPE.interpretation: 16 explicit per-octet timestamps move with the cumulative ACK queue. MSS=4, one timer, FIN has its own timestamp. Immediate handshake responses and SYN timeout history remain outside this new ledger. Existing RTT estimator, connection states and serial arithmetic are reused.

SYN-TX-AGE.interpretation: Record the latest actual SYN sequence-space send, including a SYNACK reply. A timer-driven SYN retransmission waits at least the current pre-backoff RTO; an early timer expiry waits without emitting, backoff, Karn retransmission marking or retry increment.

SYN-IMMEDIATE-REPLY.interpretation: An immediate simultaneous-open SYNACK response remains a required reply, not a timer expiry. Record its actual send time and reset the shared retransmission deadline for the replacement reply, without extending the user timeout, so the subsequent timeout cannot retransmit it prematurely.

SYN-HISTORY-SCOPE.interpretation: One SYN control position and one shared rtx timer. Preserve the finite data/FIN ledger, RTT/Karn semantics and user-timeout priority. Timer waiting is explicit; no new sequence conversion or host callbacks.

ACK-DELAY.interpretation: RFC 9293 MUST-40 bounds ACK delay below 500ms; SHLD-18/19 support delayed ACK and ACK at least every second full-sized segment or 2*RMSS new bytes. Choose a fixed first-segment deadline of 40ms (configurable 1..499ms), RMSS=4, independent of the sender RTO.

ACK-GAP.interpretation: Out-of-order, duplicate/overlapping, gap-filling, clipped, FIN or zero-window arrivals retain immediate cumulative ACK. Only fully accepted in-order data with no queued gap or FIN is eligible for deferral.

ACK-SCOPE.interpretation: Reuse parent data/ACK-window/FIN/RTO/SYN semantics. Delay only plain data in ESTABLISHED/FIN-WAIT-1/FIN-WAIT-2; a real outgoing ACK of current RCV.NXT cancels the pending ACK, including piggyback, window update and FIN. No callback protocol actions, ACK decimation, GRO, congestion control or universal output/timing proof.

PERSIST-ZWP.interpretation: MUST-36/37: probe a zero window using at least one available new or retransmitted octet and allow continued zero-window acknowledgments without a probe retry limit. SHLD-29/30: start after a current-RTO interval of queued zero-window demand; exponentially increase later probe intervals.

PERSIST-OWNERSHIP.interpretation: Enter from no flight and queued data. Use shared UNA/NXT/rtx_buf and per-byte history, never a separate sequence space. Persist owns at most one probe octet with RTO disabled; valid positive-window updates transfer remaining flight to RTO. Replace the parent all-flight-is-RTO invariant with explicit mutually exclusive ownership, retaining the ordinary case.

PERSIST-SCOPE.interpretation: One connection, 16-byte capacity, RMSS/MSS=4 parent model. Independent 1..60 second exponential persist interval; no probe RTT sample, no RTO backoff/retry increment. In-flight shrink-to-zero remains the parent RTO subset; FIN-only zero-window probing, resource/user timeout and congestion recovery remain outside this new slice.

CC-WINDOW.interpretation: RFC5681 September2009 sections2/3.1: new data bounded by min(cwnd,rwnd). One SMSS=4 conservative IW; configurable 4..16. SYN/SYNACK acknowledgments do not grow cwnd.

CC-GROWTH.interpretation: Section3.1 eq(2): slow-start increment min(newly acknowledged data bytes,SMSS). At cwnd>=ssthresh use acknowledged-byte counting; on reaching pre-ACK cwnd add one SMSS and reset credit to zero conservatively. No growth for invalid/old/duplicate/control-only ACKs or zero-window/persist probe epochs.
CC-GROWTH.strength: explicit finite slow start and byte-counting congestion avoidance

CC-LOSS.interpretation: Section3.1 eq(4): first actual positive-window data timeout for oldest byte sets ssthresh=max(floor(FlightSize/2),2*SMSS), cwnd=SMSS. Repeated timeout of that byte preserves ssthresh. Per-byte timeout marks shift with actual acknowledged data; zero-window probes and early-wait timer firings do not count as congestion loss.

CC-SOURCE.interpretation: Module-local official RFC version and raw-byte SHA256 binding; the existing global source manifest and old profiles are unchanged.

CC-SCOPE.interpretation: Parent budget, growth, timeout and persist properties retained; this overlay adds explicit finite Reno recovery. Remaining exclusions are preserved in model scope and source documentation.

FR-ACK-PHASE.interpretation: August2022 section3.10.7.4: receiver-sequence and ACK validation precede accepted-window metadata. Rejected sequence or future ACK must not replace the last accepted wire window or its validity. Reuse the explicit parent seg_acceptable and ack_is_future decisions.

FR-SOURCE.interpretation: Pinned full official RFC5681 and RFC6298 texts, versions and sections for this finite recovery model.

FR-DUPLICATE.interpretation: September2009 section2: accepted pure ACK, outstanding data, no SYN/FIN/text, ACK=UNA, wire window equals last accepted ACK-bearing wire window. Invalid/future segments ignored; window updates/data/FIN do not increment. Positive cached send window as well as positive wire window and no persist are explicit scope guards. Counts reset on new UNA, actual congestion RTO, no flight or connection cleanup.

FR-RETRANSMIT.interpretation: Section3.2 steps2/3: third duplicate ACK retransmits oldest prefix without consuming sequence space or waiting for RTO; ssthresh=max(floor(FlightSize/2),2SMSS), cwnd=ssthresh+3SMSS. Extra duplicate ACK inflates by SMSS without retransmitting again.

FR-EXIT.interpretation: Section3.2 step6: first ACK advancing UNA exits Reno, deflates to ssthresh, clears CA credit without extra SS/CA growth. Partial ACK exits too: not NewReno. Actual congestion RTO leaves recovery with parent loss window.

FR-KARN.interpretation: Section3 Karn ambiguity applies also to fast retransmission. Update actual per-byte send times and overlapped sample ambiguity; do not increment RTO retries/backoff or relabel fast recovery as timer retransmission. Keep existing RTO deadline; parent byte-age rule defers an early expiry after the fast send.

FR-SCOPE.interpretation: MSS4/queue16; explicit app.transmit new-data scheduling; no limited transmit, automatic new-data emission on each duplicate, idle restart, ECN/SACK/NewReno, FIN-only fast recovery or complete TCP proof. Legacy FIN lacks wire window and invalidates last-window knowledge.
